claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially homogenized as a high-temperature BCC phase.
Local atomic short-range ordering develops in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 during slow cooling.
Moderate-temperature thermal exposure permits local atomic short-range ordering in this alloy.
The proposed short-range order consists of clustering of particular atomic species and precedes formation of an ordered or compositionally distinct secondary phase.
Atomic diffusion during slow cooling or moderate thermal exposure facilitates short-range ordering.
Short-range ordering locally lowers free energy and destabilizes the BCC lattice.
Destabilization associated with short-range ordering drives nucleation of an alternative phase such as FCC or B2.
Rapid quenching suppresses the atomic rearrangements required for short-range ordering.
Suppressing atomic rearrangements by rapid quenching retains a relatively uniform BCC structure.
Relative to rapidly quenched samples, slowly cooled or appropriately held samples should exhibit secondary phases and associated local compositional modulations.
XRD, TEM/SAED, and APT can be used to distinguish phase formation and local compositional variation between the thermal treatments.
If the hold temperature is too low for appreciable atomic mobility, ordering and the proposed transformation mechanism should not occur.
The proposed mechanism should not apply to compositions lacking sufficient thermodynamic driving force for ordering.
A lack of secondary-phase or local-ordering differences between quenched and slowly cooled samples would falsify the proposed ordering-driven transformation under the tested conditions.
